target_customer: Off-grid rural and peri-urban households in West Africa (pay-as-you-go solar)
problem: Rural households lack grid electricity and affordable quality solar products.

founders.name: Nilmi Senaratna
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: led company through YC, scaled team to 230+ staff, now strategic board advisor in London.

technical_complexity.rationale: Distribution and consumer financing of third-party solar kits; operational and credit-collection complexity more than novel technology (no source details the stack).

defensibility.rationale: Local distribution and customer base in Senegal; 60,000+ systems sold by 2020 per press, but products and PAYG model were not unique.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in sources; Ignite Power acquired Oolu in April 2024.

market_need_then: Off-grid households in West Africa had no grid access; the company reported 60,000+ solar home systems sold by 2020, evidencing demand. No 2015-dated demand data was gathered.
outcome_analysis: Oolu raised a seed in 2015, a $3.2M Series A in 2017 and an $8.5M Series B in 2020 from impact and energy investors, sold 60,000+ systems by 2020, and grew to 230+ employees before being acquired by Ignite Power in April 2024 at an undisclosed price. The acquisition gave the buyer access to more markets; whether it was a strong or soft exit is not stated in the sources.
notes: Seed and Series A details come from search-result summaries (pages not fetched). CB Insights total $11.82M is below sum of reported rounds. Seed amount unknown. Competition not evidenced; left empty. strong_pmf and capital_efficiency tags are weakly supported.
